schema.description: Getting home from a trip, one row in a records file (source records). Closes the travel.trip series; values are the row's own text. Named place.trip.returned (v1) until card 196.

basis.description: Why the return date is believed, in the extraction's own words rather than the source's; every returned row carries one. Usually the flight that landed home, written as "<flight> arrived <d Mon>"; otherwise the documents the date rests on, which day was taken when the source printed two, or a reasoned estimate that starts "inferred:". Read it before trusting the date.
examples: inferred: ZX442 left Porthaven on 10 Mar, about 30 hours to Lakeport

date.description: The day of return. Sydney local date, YYYY-MM-DD, as the records row writes it. This is the fact time.

id.description: The row id the records file assigns, chosen once. The travel history writes it as <origin>:<trip>/<kind>, with the date and a place or route appended where a trip has several rows of a kind. This is the identity.

to.description: The city the trip returned to, as written.

trip.description: The trip key every row of one trip shares (departed, arrived, returned, flight), written by the extraction as the year and month of departure and a short slug. It names the travel.trip series. This row closes it.
